subject: Invoice consolidation, PO line tagging, and net-terms for annual commit
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aurorahealth.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2027-02-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Procurement: PO line-level requirements + net-terms request

Hi Ethan,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Aurora is excited about Redwood's latency and cost profile. Before we finalize the commercial terms, Procurement has two non-negotiable asks I need to surface: 

1) PO and invoice formatting: our ERP requires line-level fields on each invoice line: 
   - cost_center (6-digit code)
   - project_code (alphanumeric)
   - vendor_sku (we will provide a mapping)
   This must be present on every invoice line or the AP system will reject it.

2) Payment terms: Aurora's standard is NET75 for cloud/SAAS vendors. This is a hard policy for our group (we have to apply the same across vendors).

Operational asks: we run weekly billing cycles per cost center; we'd like consolidated invoices (one invoice per week) rather than monthly. Will Redwood support a weekly consolidated invoice that includes the above line-level fields?

Commercial ask: if we commit to a $600k annual spend (forecasted), can Redwood provide a tiered discount (we're targeting a floor of 6–8% off list) and would any of that discount be applied as consumption credits versus upfront?

I've attached our PO template so you can see required fields (Aurora_PO_template.xlsx). Also, Procurement will need evidence of SOC2 compliance before we proceed.

Appreciate a quick confirmation on whether the PO line requirements and NET75 are feasible, and who on your side I should coordinate finance/ops with.

Best,
Liam O'Connor
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Aurora Health


From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-02-16T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Procurement: PO line-level requirements + net-terms request

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear summary and the PO template. Looping in Vanessa (account lead) and Marissa (finance ops) so they can comment on pricing and invoice mechanics.

Short answer: we should be able to support line-level tagging and weekly consolidated invoices, but NET75 is outside of our standard AR cadence and may require an approval path. Vanessa and Marissa — can you weigh in with recommended commercial compromises and operational steps?

I'll hold off on approving anything until we get finance's read.

Thanks,
Ethan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

On 2027-02-16 09:12, Liam O'Connor wrote:
> (see below)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-02-16T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Procurement: PO line-level requirements + net-terms request

Hi Liam — great to meet you over email. Appreciate the upfront details; helps us scope how to onboard your AP flow. A few operational and commercial notes from our side: 

Operational feasibility
- Weekly consolidated invoices: yes — we can generate one consolidated invoice per week per billing entity. To do line-level mapping reliably we need the PO to include "cost_center" and "project_code" fields matching the attached mapping. We can also accept a CSV from your system each week that maps usage lines to your cost centers.
- Required fields on invoice lines: we will include vendor_sku, project_code, cost_center as custom invoice line attributes. Your team will need to confirm the exact column headers (case-sensitive).

Payment terms & AR
- NET75: outside of our standard (net30/net45) and will require AR & finance approval plus a credit review. If you must have NET75, we can pursue it as an exception but would ask for one of the following: 1) a contract amendment committing Aurora to an annual minimum spend (we can document $600k), or 2) an early-pay discount tier.

Discount options (examples)
- Option A: 7% volume discount on annual committed consumption of >= $600k, invoiced monthly with weekly reconciliation files.
- Option B: 5% standard discount at $300k commit; additional 2% applied as consumption credits on a quarterly true-up.
- Option C: keep NET60 (compromise) + 1.5% early-pay discount if invoices paid within 30 days.

Packaging note: if Aurora requires billing across multiple legal entities, we can support multi-entity billing but it requires billing entity setup and may add a 2-week lead time.

I've attached a draft mutual action plan that captures these options (Redwood_MAPlan_v1.pdf). Marissa — can you outline the specific AR approval steps for NET75?

Liam — would you be open to NET60 + a 6–7% committed discount (Option A), or do you need NET75 as a hard constraint?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@aurorahealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2027-02-17T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Procurement: PO line-level requirements + net-terms request

Hi Vanessa, Ethan — thanks for the quick responses. A couple clarifications from Procurement/Finance at Aurora: 

1) NET75 is policy for cloud/SaaS vendors and cannot be shortened without a procurement waiver; we can request a waiver but it typically takes 2–3 business days and needs commercial approval. Can Redwood accept NET75 conditionally if we provide a purchase order referencing an annual commitment and a standard vendor credit reference?

2) Weekly consolidated invoices are required — our AP runs a weekly pay cycle per cost center. If Redwood can provide a weekly invoice plus an attached CSV that maps each invoice line to our ERP fields, that will work operationally.

3) Regarding discounts: our preference is to have discounts applied as credits (consumption credits) that appear on the invoice so the AP system can process net amounts. Front-loading discounts into pre-paid credits is acceptable as well.

I've attached a completed sample PO for your team to test against (attached: Aurora_PO_template_filled.xlsx). Also please upload your redacted SOC2 report so our security team can triage.

Best,
Sarah Kim
Procurement Manager
Aurora Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@aurorahealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-02-17T14:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Procurement: PO line-level requirements + net-terms request

Hi Sarah/Vanessa/Ethan — operational note from Finance Ops:

We can map Aurora's PO fields into our invoice template, but we need a consistent column header set and a sample weekly CSV extract that will accompany each invoice. Minimum required columns we need from your CSV: invoice_date, invoice_id (we will generate), cost_center, project_code, vendor_sku, quantity, unit_price, total_line_amount.

NET75 approvals: this is an exception that requires sign-off from our Credit Committee. To expedite, please provide: 
  - three vendor credit references OR a corporate credit profile,
  - the signed PO referencing the annual commitment, and
  - confirmation of the billing entity/legal name for tax paperwork.

Temporary workaround while approvals are processed: Redwood can issue monthly invoices with weekly CSV usage files (one consolidated CSV per week) so your AP team can post weekly entries — this avoids retooling our invoice conduit while you get the waiver approved. Once NET75 is approved we can switch the invoice cadence to weekly.

Attaching a redacted SOC2 snapshot for your security team (SOC2_report_redacted.pdf).

Next operational steps I need from Aurora:
- Completed sample CSV for one pay cycle (this week)
- Signed PO with billing-entity legal name
- Credit references (if you can, send by EOD Friday)

Marissa Cole
Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aurorahealth.com>, Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-02-18T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Procurement: PO line-level requirements + net-terms request — proposed compromise & next steps

Hi Sarah/Liam — thanks for the quick turnaround and for sending the filled PO. To move this forward and avoid multi-week delays, Redwood can propose the following compromise for signature next week: 

1) Invoice cadence: Redwood will issue weekly consolidated invoices to Aurora with a single invoice per week per billing entity. Each weekly invoice will include an attached CSV mapping file containing cost_center and project_code for every line.

2) PO / line-level requirements: We will include vendor_sku, cost_center, and project_code as invoice line attributes; Aurora will confirm exact header casing for the CSV.

3) Payment terms: Redwood will accept NET65 as a one-time commercial compromise (we will submit the NET75 waiver request but ask Aurora to accept NET65 in the MSA amendment to expedite onboarding). 

4) Discounts / packaging: For an annual committed spend >= $600,000 we will provide a 6% committed discount applied as consumption credits on invoices (applied quarterly as a true-up). Alternatively, if Aurora prefers an early-pay incentive, we can offer NET60 + 1.5% early-pay discount — choose your preferred mechanism in the amendment.

5) Next steps: 
   - I will circulate an MSA amendment with the NET65/discount option and wiring instructions: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC-987654
   - Marissa will validate the sample CSV once you send it this week.
   - Security evidence: SOC2_report_redacted.pdf uploaded to the Share (attached) and will be available to your security team.

If that compromise is acceptable, please confirm and we'll route the amendment for signature and start billing setup. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you want to run through the CSV mapping.

Appreciate the speedy collaboration — hoping we can get Aurora live in March.

Thanks,
Ethan Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
